bull_bear.body: Priority 1: New store openings in cluster approach. Priority 2: Strategic inventory procurement to hedge against OEM price hikes/supply shocks. Priority 3: Balance sheet strengthening. No dividends or buybacks highlighted; reinvestment mode.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Execution risk in new states (UP/MP/Chhattisgarh) vs Bihar maturity; Supply chain disruptions (Gulf war impact on gas/components); Real estate rental inflation (though currently stable in target regions); Margin recovery dependency on normalizing summer demand for cooling category.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and resilient. Emphasizes transition to 'all-weather' business model. Defensive on specific margin data (state-wise/mature vs new) citing competition, but clear on strategic intent to prioritize market share over short-term margin spikes during price hikes.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Inventory buildup (INR 840cr) is a deliberate arbitrage play on anticipated OEM price hikes (8-10%) and supply constraints, not just demand buffering. The 'weak' FY26 actually accelerated the maturity curve by forcing reliance on non-summer quarters, proving the H2 growth engine.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Balance sheet framed as conservative: 'Low debt balance sheet', 'Operates on a cash-and-carry model' and 'Efficient inventory management and high cash reserves'.
- Deleveraging shown on the FY22-FY26 charts: the 'Net Debt to EBITDA (x)' series reads 1.5, 1.4, 0.2, 0.7, 0.3 and 'Net Debt to Equity (x)' reads 1.6, 1.4, 0.1, 0.2, 0.1.
- Growth has been part-funded by equity: FY2024 saw the 'First fund raise after IPO from the one of the World's largest FII - Capital Group'.
- Receivables are structurally negligible - the deck notes 'Receivable Days are less than 0 since the Company has negligible Trade Receivables' - so working capital is inventory and payables driven.
- No dividend policy, buyback or payout commentary appears anywhere in the deck.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Cooling (AC/Coolers/Fridges): Margin dilution in H1 due to weak summer, expected recovery in H2/FY27. Mobile/Laptops: Volume surge with significant ASP inflation (Mobile +20%, Laptop +8-10%), driving revenue but compressing blended gross margin (15.6% FY26 vs historical higher levels). Small Appliances: ~50% growth noted. Geography: Bihar (74% Q4 rev), UP (14%), Jharkhand (12%).
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Supply chain constraints and raw material (gas) shortages leading to OEM price hikes | Voltas | beneficiary | Med | Aditya's strategic stocking indicates anticipated strong demand and price firmness in AC segment, benefiting manufacturers with pricing power. |
| Rural/semi-urban consumption recovery lagging in broader indices | Titan Company | beneficiary | Low | While Aditya focuses on durables, the confirmed rise in disposable income in Bihar/UP/Jharkhand supports broader discretionary spending, though direct correlation is weaker. |
| Intense competition in mobile/laptop segment compressing retailer margins | Vijaya Diagnostic Centre | loser | Low | Unrelated sector, but if consumer wallet share shifts heavily to high-ASP electronics due to inflation, discretionary health spend could face headwinds in these specific geographies. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Deck claims '50%+ Mkt Share' in Bihar 'as per Crisil Report' and 'Largest Electronic Retailer in Jharkhand', plus '1st Consumer Electronics Retailer To be listed' (BSE 2016, NSE 2024).
- 'Zero Store Closure since Inception' since the first Patna store in FY1999; 100% retail sales with no private labels, purely a multi-brand retailer of 100+ OEM brands.
- Frames its addressable base as the Hindi heartland: Bihar, Jharkhand, UP and Chhattisgarh together '~31% of India's Estimated Population' (deck's per-state figures: UP 24 Cr, Bihar 13 Cr, Jharkhand 4 Cr, Chhattisgarh 3 Cr).
- Positions physical stores as structurally advantaged for premium, high-ticket purchases - 'physical stores help enhancing the perception of a brand', 'high-touch customer experience', and 'Good after sale service plays a major role while buying a high-ticket item'.
- Rides an organised-sector shift: deck cites organised share of consumer durables retail moving from 49% (FY16) / 58% (FY21) to 77% (FY27P) per CRISIL Research.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Demand environment] Q1 FY27 demand was weather-split: 'East remained 5-8 degrees C cooler than North/Central during most of April & May', with Bihar and Jharkhand seeing intermittent rain and softer demand while UP's sustained heat supported cooling demand.
- [Consumer sentiment] Deck argues 'Sentiment, not income, became the key constraint', citing public messaging on gold read as a cue to 'Spend Less, Save More', LPG cylinder availability concerns, and a Rs 1,000 petrol pump purchase limit that led households to preserve cash.
- [Governance] Board is promoter-heavy at the executive level (Chairman & MD Yashovardhan Sinha, two promoter whole-time directors, two promoter non-executive directors) against six independent directors including ex-Samsung India and ex-UCO Bank veterans.
- [Demographics] Deck notes India's fertility has fallen below replacement (TFR 1.9) while its target states remain above it - Bihar 2.9, Uttar Pradesh 2.6, Madhya Pradesh 2.4, Chhattisgarh 2.2, Jharkhand 2.1.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Gross Margin: 16% (Q4), 15.6% (FY26). EBITDA Margin: 8.1% (Q4), 8.5% (FY26). Pressure from low-margin high-ASP mobile/laptop mix. Operating expenses rose due to expansion freight, credit card commissions, and brand ambassador fees. Management expects opex to stabilize as new store % declines relative to mature base.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Continuing robust trajectory (April described as 'very robust'); Margin: Target range 8%-10% (striving for 9%); Order Inflow: N/A; Capex/Commissioning: ~25-30+ new stores annually (calibrated cluster approach), focusing on UP, Chhattisgarh, and entry into Madhya Pradesh.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: N/A - Retail business model relies on inventory turnover rather than order book. Inventory held at INR 840cr (strategically high) to secure pre-hike pricing and ensure availability for strong summer demand.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Deepening penetration in UP (only 30/75 districts covered); New state entry: Chhattisgarh (3 stores), Madhya Pradesh (planned FY27), and a previously withheld neighboring state now politically stable. Mature store mix improvement as >50% of stores cross 3-year mark.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Aditya Vision successfully pivoted from a H1-heavy seasonal model to an all-weather performer, delivering 28% Q4 revenue growth despite a weak summer, driven by strategic inventory stocking ahead of OEM price hikes and accelerated expansion in Uttar Pradesh. The shift in product mix toward higher-ASP but lower-margin mobiles/laptops compressed reported margins, masking the underlying operating leverage maturing stores will provide in FY27.

open.item: Do not foresee raising any equity capital this financial year or near-term; internal accruals plus short-term working-capital borrowings sufficient for expansion and inventory.
Company plans to add more than 30 stores per year (guides conservatively at 25) via calibrated cluster expansion; will not give a firm number.
On track to enter Madhya Pradesh this financial year (FY27), having already entered Chhattisgarh with 3 stores earlier than planned; a neighbouring state also opening up for expansion.
Store expansion is anchored in sustaining strong double-digit Same-Store Sales Growth (SSSG).
The Company plans to add at least 25–30 stores annually over the next 2–3 years, building on a network of 207 stores as of March 31, 2026.
Strategy to make newer states (UP, Chhattisgarh, MP) gradually catch up to Bihar's mature-state margins over time without compromising sales.
The Company is focusing on scaling premium and sunrise categories to enhance per-store economics.
Stores get to breakeven between 9 and 12 months from opening (mature by ~3 years).
As ~50% of stores cross 3 years and fewer new stores are added in percentage terms, management expects better control over operating expenses and a margin lever near-term.
Management claims the business is now an all-weather, all-season company, with H2 becoming as important as H1 (previously Q1/Q2 were 55-60% of annual sales).
Endeavour to reach back toward 9% EBITDA margin; standing guidance range of 8% to 10%.
Company will not sell private-label products as per policy; sells only branded stock.
Reiterated long-term potential of around 500 stores across current states over a long horizon.
New store revenue model of ~Rs.6 crore in first year, Rs.12 crore in second, Rs.18 crore in third year is broadly holding, with many stores doing better than guided.

verdicts.item: Company guides to adding around 25 to 30 stores per year.
verdicts.note: Store count rose from 175 to 207 (~32 added in FY26) - at/above the 25-30 annual pace.

verdicts.item: Expand from Eastern UP into Central UP and later Western UP, with entry into Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh planned in FY25-26.
verdicts.note: "We have entered Chhattisgarh earlier than planned with 3 stores" and Western UP expansion underway; Madhya Pradesh still pending ("on track to enter Madhya Pradesh this financial year").

verdicts.item: Currently focusing expansion only in Uttar Pradesh; will update on additional territories by end of H1FY26.
verdicts.note: The promised additional-territory move executed - "We have entered Chhattisgarh earlier than planned with 3 stores," with MP next.

verdicts.item: Flagged unseasonal rains and slow market at start of Q1FY26 with growth only in single digits so far, though management expects recovery.
verdicts.note: The expected recovery from the weak Q1 played out - the year concluded with 18% growth and "your company is now an all-weather, all-season company."

verdicts.item: No national marketing campaign planned; will keep marketing regional given culturally similar Bihar/Jharkhand/UP markets.
verdicts.note: "we have onboarded Pankaj Tripathi as our brand ambassador" - a step-up in brand-building beyond the earlier no-national-marketing stance, though positioned for "our core markets."

verdicts.item: On track to add 25 to 30 new stores in FY26, aiming to cross the 200-plus store milestone by year-end.
verdicts.note: "we close FY26 with 207 stores" - crossed the 200-store milestone with ~32 added in FY26.

verdicts.item: Guidance to add minimum 25, and 25-30 stores in FY26, mostly in H2 (fewer in lean Q1).
verdicts.note: ~32 stores added in FY26 (bulk in H2, only ~2 in Q1) - met/exceeded the 25-30 H2-weighted plan.

verdicts.item: Team remains confident of achieving ~20% to 25% sales growth guidance despite the washout Q1.
verdicts.note: FY26 revenue grew 18%, short of the 20-25% the team expressed confidence in achieving (weak-summer washout Q1); framed as "quite respectable" but below guidance. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Full-year FY26 SSSG expected to be in positive territory despite Q1 SSSG of minus 4%.
verdicts.note: "Same-store sales growth for FY26 stood at 8%" - positive full-year SSSG achieved despite the Q1 minus 4%.

verdicts.item: Current expansion focus remains Uttar Pradesh (moving to Western UP); not focusing on any other state right now.
verdicts.note: UP/Western UP focus continues, but the company has now expanded beyond UP into Chhattisgarh (and MP next), evolving past the earlier UP-only stance.

verdicts.item: Chhattisgarh entry not happening in H1FY26 but on the agenda; may take a call to enter by Q4FY26.
verdicts.note: "We have entered Chhattisgarh earlier than planned with 3 stores" - Chhattisgarh entry executed within FY26.

verdicts.item: Optimistic on festive season and H2FY26 demand driven by good monsoon/bumper harvest, Bihar 125-unit free electricity scheme and income tax relief tailwinds.
verdicts.note: The H2FY26 optimism borne out - "we did extremely well in Q3 FY26 with a top line growth of 28%... The momentum further accelerated in Q4 FY26... another robust top line growth of 28%."
